verses.text: Suppose a man marries a woman, but she does not please him because he finds something shameful about her. He writes her a certificate of divorce, gives it to her, and sends her away from his house.
After she leaves his house, she may become another man's wife.
Then her second husband may also turn against her, write her a certificate of divorce, give it to her, and send her away from his house. Or her second husband may die.

In either case, her first husband, who divorced her, is not allowed to marry her again, because she has been made unclean. That would be hateful to the LORD. Do not bring sin on the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.
If a man has just married, he must not be sent to war or given any other duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and make his new wife happy.
Do not take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper millstone, as a guarantee for a loan. That would be taking away a person's way of making a living.
If someone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating them as a slave or selling them, the kidnapper must die. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
If there is an outbreak of a serious skin disease, be very careful to do exactly what the priests, who are Levites, teach you. Be careful to do what I have commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on your journey after you left Egypt.
When you lend your neighbour anything, do not go into their house to take the thing they offer as a guarantee.
Stay outside, and let the person you are lending to bring it out to you.
If the person is poor, do not go to sleep while keeping their guarantee.
Be sure to give their cloak back by sunset so that they can sleep in it. Then they will bless you, and the LORD your God will see it as a right thing you have done.
Do not take advantage of a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether they are a fellow Israelite or a foreigner living in one of your towns.
Pay them their wages each day before sunset, because they are poor and are counting on it. Otherwise they may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Parents must not be put to death for what their children have done, and children must not be put to death for what their parents have done. Each person must die for their own sin.
Do not deny justice to foreigners or orphans, and do not take a widow's cloak as a guarantee for a loan.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the LORD your God set you free from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you are gathering your harvest in your field and you forget a bundle of grain, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows, so that the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches a second time. Leave what remains for the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows.
When you pick the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over the vines a second time. Leave what remains for the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
